title: Romance, marriage and divorce
subtitle: a date, get engaged, a honeymoon
summary: Tell the story of a relationship in English - a first date, going out with someone, getting engaged, the wedding, and sometimes a divorce.

lesson.heading: Romance
lesson.text: A **date** is a planned romantic meeting. If you **go out with** someone, you have a romantic relationship with them. When the relationship ends, you **break up**.

examples.text: I had my first **date** when I was 16, and it was terrible.
When I was 17, I **went out with** a girl for three months.
We **broke up** when she met a boy who had a car.
My first **serious relationship** was when I went to university.

lesson.heading: Falling in love
lesson.text: You **get to know** someone when you slowly become friends with them. If you decide to marry, you **get engaged**. **A couple of** means two, perhaps three.

examples.text: I **got to know** Melanie because we were on the same course.
At first we were just friends, then we started going out with each other.
After a few months we realised we were **in love**.
We **got engaged** **a couple of** years after we left university.
examples.note: get engaged = formally agree to marry

lesson.heading: Marriage
lesson.text: **Marriage** is the time when you are married. The **wedding** is the ceremony when two people **get married**. On the day, the woman is the **bride** and the man is the **bridegroom** (usually just **groom**).

examples.text: We **got married** the following year.
examples.note: get married = become husband and wife

examples.text: We didn't want a big **ceremony**, so we had the **wedding** in the local church.
examples.note: a ceremony is an important public event

examples.text: Afterwards we had the **reception** in a small hotel nearby.
Then we went on our **honeymoon** to Greece.
examples.note: a honeymoon = a holiday just after getting married

lesson.text: Say *They plan to get married*, not ~~get marry~~ or ~~get married with~~. We marry **to** a person: *She's getting married to Darren next year.*

lesson.heading: Children
lesson.text: When a woman is going to have a baby, she is **pregnant**. A baby **is born**. An **anniversary** is a day exactly one or more years after an important event, and a **celebration** is a time when you do something you enjoy because the day is special.

examples.text: Three years later Melanie got **pregnant**.
Our first child, Cal, **was born** two days after our fourth wedding **anniversary**.
We had a big **celebration**.

lesson.heading: Divorce
lesson.text: A **divorce** is when a marriage officially ends. Before that, things often **go wrong** [become a problem]. If you **give up** a job, you stop doing it. **On your own** means alone.

examples.text: Things started to **go wrong** when I got a job as a manager.
At weekends she was often alone, **on her own** with two young children.
I felt I couldn't **give up** my job.
examples.note: give something up = stop doing it

examples.text: In the end Melanie decided to **leave** me.
examples.note: leave someone = stop living with them

examples.text: The following year we **got divorced**.

exercises.prompt: The big party you have after the wedding is the ___.
exercises.explanation: The wedding party is called the reception.

exercises.prompt: A romantic meeting you plan before it happens is a ___.
exercises.explanation: A planned romantic meeting is a date.

exercises.prompt: How do we describe a woman who is going to have a baby?
exercises.explanation: A woman who is going to have a baby is pregnant. The noun is pregnancy.

exercises.prompt: They got engaged last week. They plan to get married in a ___ of years.
exercises.explanation: a couple of years = two, perhaps three years.

exercises.prompt: Match each explanation with the word or phrase it defines.

pairs.left: the woman on her wedding day
the man on his wedding day
a day exactly one or more years after an important event
stop doing a job or an activity
the period of time when you are married
the holiday just after getting married

exercises.prompt: *A:* Where did they meet? *B:* I think he got ___ her at university.
exercises.explanation: get to know someone = slowly become friends with them.

exercises.statement: She knew Darren at university, and now they are getting married.
exercises.explanation: She got to know Darren at university, and now they are getting married.

exercises.prompt: It isn't going to be a big wedding. They're having a small ___ in the village church.
exercises.explanation: The wedding ceremony is the formal part of the day.

exercises.prompt: Put the events of the relationship in a logical order.
words: I met Gabriel at a party.
exercises.answer: I met Gabriel at a party. I got to know Gabriel. I went out with Gabriel. We got engaged. We got married. We went on our honeymoon.
exercises.explanation: You meet someone, get to know them, go out with them, get engaged, get married, and then go on honeymoon.

exercises.prompt: So it's all over. Lily ___ him and moved out last month.
exercises.explanation: leave someone = stop living with them.

exercises.prompt: Have they had problems for a long time? I think it all started to go ___ when they moved to Woodbridge.
*A:* Is Oliver alone now? *B:* Yes, completely on ___. He doesn't want a new relationship yet.
Their marriage is definitely over and it is ending officially. What are they doing?
exercises.explanation: A divorce is when a marriage officially ends.
